bullets.title: TSMC smashes Q2, raises FY26 guide to >40% rev growth; capex jumps to $60-64B
bullets.body: TSMC reported Q2 EPS of $4.31 (beat vs $3.95 est), revenue $40.2B (beat vs $39.3B est), and Q3 guide of $45.2B vs $43B consensus. FY26 revenue growth guidance raised to >40% YoY (vs prior >30%), capex raised to $60-64B from $52-56B on AI demand and higher equipment costs. N2 ramp diluting 2H gross margins by 3-4pts, guiding Q3 GM to ~66% vs 67.7% in Q2 — the one blemish. TSMC also announced an additional $100B Arizona investment for 2nm fabs, bringing total US commitment to $265B.

bullets.title: AI capex momentum unwind: semis/SOX -2%+ despite TSMC strength; memory hardest hit
bullets.body: Despite TSMC's fundamental beat, the SOX and networking indices fell 2-5% as markets digested elevated expectations and gross margin miss. Memory names led the decline: HYNIX -10%, SAMSUNG -7%, KIOXIA -15% overnight; MU -4.7%, WDC -7.3%, SNDK -6.8%, STX -6.1% pre-market. MS notes a tech momentum index down -24% since June 22, below historical peak-to-trough median. Semi-cap equipment also under pressure (LRCX -3.7%, AMAT -3.3%, COHR -5.1%).

bullets.title: Memory is the next AI binding constraint; agentic AI could drive 26-77% of incremental DRAM demand by 2030
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley estimates memory could rise from 12% of cloud capex in 2023 to 40% by 2027 as the AI bottleneck shifts from compute to memory. Goldman Sachs separately sees AI agents driving a 24x increase in token consumption by 2030, worsening near-term chip shortages over the next 12-18 months. Bipartisan US lawmakers are pushing the Trump administration to ban US purchases of Chinese memory chips from CXMT and YMTC.

bullets.title: NVDA CEO Huang: 'We are still at the beginning of the cycle'; Japan AI factory with 27,500 Rubin GPUs announced
bullets.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang reiterated the industry is early-cycle at today's event, implying extended AI demand runway. Simultaneously, NVDA announced a partnership with Noetra to build Japan's national AI factory deploying 13,750 Vera CPUs and 27,500 Rubin GPUs at 140MW capacity — described as the first national-scale AI factory of its kind globally. Oppenheimer also highlighted NVDA's 2H VR200 ramp extending its performance lead.

bullets.title: Citi raises GOOGL/META/AMZN 2027 capex projections 12-22%; hyperscalers collectively on track for $725B+ spend
bullets.body: Citi raised GOOGL 2027E capex by ~21% to $308B (stronger TPU/GCP demand, negative FCF by '27-'28), META by ~22% to $205B (~14GW compute capacity), and AMZN by ~12% to $288B. AWS projected +32.5% YoY in Q2 and +40% YoY in 2027. MS pegs 2027 AI capex consensus at $1.1T, with Goldman expecting hyperscaler capex increases likely in 2027. JPM notes the four biggest US AI operators expected to spend $725B+ this year.

bullets.title: US macro backdrop solid across the board: retail sales, jobless claims, Philly Fed all beat
bullets.body: June retail sales rose 8.4% YoY (control group +0.54% MoM, 6.4% YoY), with sporting goods +17.8%, e-commerce +18%, consumer electronics +10.5%. Initial jobless claims fell to 208K (2-month low), 13-week average down 8.3% YoY. Philly Fed manufacturing surged 31pts MoM to an ISM-equivalent of 58.1, highest since late 2021; Empire State manufacturing ISM-adjusted hit 57.5. Morgan Stanley revised 2Q real consumption up 0.3pt to 2.4% and 2Q GDP up 0.2pt to 1.7%.

bullets.title: PPI goods fell sharply m/m in June; portfolio management component soft, lowering PCE estimates
bullets.body: June PPI saw a massive m/m decline in goods while services ticked modestly higher. The portfolio management sub-component came in surprisingly soft, pulling PCE price index estimates lower. Despite the benign headline, prices for processed intermediate materials continue to rise rapidly, suggesting consumer goods inflation could accelerate in coming months. El-Erian separately commented that 'most of the inflation we were worried about is now in the rearview mirror.'

bullets.title: South Korea BOK hikes 25bps to 2.75% amid stagflation; Kospi plunges 6.4%, DRAM sector -25.2% from peak
bullets.body: The Bank of Korea raised rates for the first time in 3.5 years (+25bps to 2.75%), triggering a 6.4% Kospi decline overnight. Hedgeye notes the DRAM sector is now down 25.2% from its cycle peak. South Korean regulators also unveiled curbs on high-risk ETFs, adding to the pressure on speculative semiconductor and AI names.

bullets.title: Middle East escalation: Iran instructs Houthis to prepare to close Bab el-Mandeb Strait; Brent at $84
bullets.body: Iran reportedly instructed Yemen's Houthis to prepare to close the Bab el-Mandeb Strait — which carries 10-12% of global maritime trade — if the US strikes Iranian power infrastructure. Iraq halted all oil loadings at Basra terminals after a drone hit a tanker (no damage). Brent crude fell 1% to $84.07/bbl as traders weigh conflict risk. Gold fell nearly 1% to $4,024/oz.

bullets.title: $2.8T in notional OI expiring in record monthly OPEX; VIX at floor levels, hedging complacent
bullets.body: This morning marks the largest monthly options expiration on record with $2.8 trillion in notional open interest set to expire. VIX sits at historical floor levels — 15.97 per pre-market data — with QQQ implied vol at a -15% discount despite NASDAQ only -3.1% from all-time highs. 22V recommends August VIX and TLT calls as cheap vol hedges into Mag 7 earnings next week.

bullets.title: Tech rotation is 42 days into an average 201-day cycle; Mag 7 earnings (GOOGL Jul 22, MSFT/META Jul 29) are next key catalyst
bullets.body: Historical precedent across 9 rotations since 2000 shows tech sector rotations averaging 201 days, suggesting ~4 more months before capital flows back to tech. Hyperscaler earnings represent the dominant near-term catalyst: GOOGL reports July 22, TSLA/TXN also July 22, MSFT and META July 29. 22V recommends staying low-conviction long Momentum and Semis into these prints with Value as a structural hedge given its 2nd-percentile correlation to Momentum.

bullets.title: TSMC Arizona $100B incremental capex confirmed; NVDA H200 chips entering China market after 6-month delay
bullets.body: TSMC's additional $100B Arizona investment (2nm and below) was confirmed by the US Commerce Department. Separately, Hedgeye reports NVDA H200 chips approved for China in January 2026 are now entering market: ~200K units at $30K/chip premium = $6B gross sales, $4.5B net after US government tax, $2.7B gross profit. Chinese H200 grey market rental rates trending higher, justifying premium pricing.

bullets.title: JPM macro outlook: structurally firmer inflation, higher term premium, tech sovereignty as new regulatory battleground
bullets.body: JPMorgan's 2H26 strategic themes note identifies structurally firmer inflation and higher term premium as leaving less room for policy errors, with financial stability risks migrating to funding markets and non-banks. Deregulation is characterized as a tailwind while tech sovereignty is the new regulatory battlefield. The firm sees deficits, deregulation, and de-carbonization as the three fastest-accelerating structural forces, and warns retail's larger S&P 500 footprint amplifies downside feedback loops.

bullets.title: EU forces Google to share search data with competitors by Jan-27 and enable Android AI interoperability by Jul-27
bullets.body: The European Commission issued two legally binding specifications under the Digital Markets Act requiring Google to share search data with eligible search engine providers starting January 2027 and to enable Android AI interoperability by July 2027. Separately, Meta was ordered to change addictive features on Facebook and Instagram, and Alphabet/Microsoft face proposed UK cloud services oversight.

bullets.title: Housing data weak: NAHB at 10-month low, pending home sales -5.4%, mortgage apps -2.7%
bullets.body: The July NAHB Housing Market Index fell to 34, tying its 10-month low, with all three sub-components declining. June pending home sales dropped 5.4% MoM vs. consensus -0.5%. Mortgage applications fell 2.7% WoW, with purchase applications down 7.3%. The effective interest rate on outstanding mortgage debt hit its highest level since end of 2011. Analysts still expect a U-shaped recovery but near-term data is uniformly weak.

bullets.title: AAPL approved to roll out Apple Intelligence in China; exploring AI semiconductor acquisitions
bullets.body: Apple received approval to roll out Apple Intelligence in China, its No. 2 market after the US. Morgan Stanley also reports AAPL is exploring AI semiconductor acquisitions, noting current M2 Ultra cannot handle the largest Google Gemini workloads. AAPL also raised AppleCare+ prices by $0.50/month and $5/year. AAPL hit a 52-week high, up 57.8% YTD.

bullets.title: Visa/Mastercard Q2 volumes accelerated ~150bps YoY, beating UBS models; World Cup adds 40-50bps to Visa FY26 revenue
bullets.body: UBS bank issuer data shows Q2 debit/credit volumes accelerated ~150bps YoY vs. models forecasting only ~50bps (V) and ~10bps (MA) acceleration. Debit grew 9.2% YoY, credit 7.7%. Travel cross-border slowed 600bps for Visa and 6ppts for Mastercard due to Middle East conflict. Visa estimates 40-50bps FY26 revenue benefit from the 2026 World Cup. Clear Street initiated both V (Buy, $403 PT) and MA (Buy, $617 PT).

bullets.title: KIMI K3 model with 2-3 trillion parameters expected tonight; Chinese AI competition intensifying
bullets.body: Chinese AI startup Moonshot is expected to unveil its K3 model tonight — an open-weight model with 2-3 trillion parameters, reportedly outperforming Anthropic's Opus 4.8 but falling short of Fable 5. Separately, Chinese AI startup Moonshot is also launching a model challenging Anthropic. AI substitution risk from cheaper Chinese models is being cited as competitive pressure on US hyperscaler AI capex leaders.

bullets.title: Section 122 tariff expiring July 24; tariff refund outflows doubled collections in June
bullets.body: JPMorgan's macro calendar flags the Section 122 tariff expiration on July 24 as a key trade policy inflection point alongside the November 1 trade truce expiration. Adding complexity, the US government paid out nearly double in tariff refunds vs. tariff revenues collected in June, reflecting the strained mechanics of current trade enforcement.

bullets.title: Japan, China equities under pressure; Japan largest foreign buyer of US stocks reducing equity exposure
bullets.body: Japan equities dropped 2.8% overnight with a Vol of Vol breakout confirmed (bearish on margin). Japan's largest foreign buyer of US stocks is reportedly reducing exposure citing valuation concerns. China equities fell 1.9% overnight to new cycle lows with a 'get out' Vol of Vol signal. Eurozone trade balance swung to a -€4.97B deficit in May vs. +€2.8B expected, adding to international risk-off sentiment.
